summary: Rework the PDF reader after owner complaints: DPR-aware canvas rendering (crisp on Retina), a page-thumbnail sidebar open by default with current-page highlighting, zoom/fit controls, lazy per-page rendering near the viewport, the official pdf.js TextLayer instead of my hand-rolled one (which mis-positioned spans and broke selection), and the vendored standard_fonts set that was missing. Adds a 浏览器打开 button for the native viewer.
scope_note: Covers the diff since commit 1cfb183, including the vendored standard_fonts (~800 KB, with their own licence files). No model call.

budget_impact.rationale: Reader UI and vendored assets only; no model call and no budget/config change.
budget_impact.before: Blurry canvas (no DPR), no sidebar, no zoom, hand-rolled text layer that broke selection, missing standard fonts.
budget_impact.after: DPR rendering, thumbnail sidebar, zoom/fit, lazy rendering, pdf.js TextLayer, standard fonts served.
budget_impact.developer_usage: unknown; host does not expose complete aggregate developer token accounting

additional_checks.command: pdf.js data path on a real 50-page paper (Node)
additional_checks.scope: PAGES 50; VIEWPORT 857x1109; TEXT_ITEMS 189 CHARS 3051; TextLayer function

reviews.reviewer: Implementing agent; UI/assets work, not recommendation quality

open_risks: Crispness, sidebar looks and selection feel are unverified visually (no completed DOM-level browser check).
CJK cmaps are not vendored, so Chinese PDFs may miss glyphs.
Very large PDFs are still not optimised.
Recommendation quality remains unproven; gates stay not_run.
